session_items.Title: Google Summer of Code Community Hub 2025
session_items.Description: The primary aim of this project will be the refactoring of a domain specific language compiler to produce Svelte components rather than React Components, in order to enable the translation of components specified using minimal syntax to robust, secure and functional web applications at scale. Multiple components will be implemented using the new svelte framework , such as a video conferencing meet-your-mentor component, and a gsoc Leaderboard component which would allow for the gamification of contributions to the Rocket.Chat community. Finally, all components will be adapted to fully meet the pre-scaled “serverless” vision for the application, so components can be specified can be specified in natural language and transformed into full fledged applications at build time. All of this will culminate in the implementation of a functional Community Hub to be used for future summers.
session_items.Speaker: Daniel Akinola

session_items.Title: Convert endpoints to new Pattern
session_items.Description: Updated Rocket.Chat APIs to adopt the OpenAPI Specification (OAS). Implemented AJV validation for request bodies, queries, and responses to ensure type safety and consistency. Integrated Swagger UI with the new OAS pattern, enabling interactive and accurate API documentation for developers. Automated the generation of OpenAPI specs, centralising each updated API into a single file containing its validation, schema, and definition, replacing scattered files across the project. Improved overall maintainability and developer experience by standardising and thoroughly documenting all updated APIs.
session_items.Speaker: Ahmed Abdel-Twab

session_items.Title: Receipts Processor and Reporting App powered by Multi-modal LLMs
session_items.Description:
This project automates receipt processing and expense reporting using OCR capabilities of multi-modal LLMs to address the time-consuming nature of manual expense tracking.

Users upload receipts into designated chat channels—each representing a specific event, time period, or trip—where the system validates the image, extracts structured data such as amount, date, and items, and categorizes expenses automatically. The processed data is stored persistently, allowing users to generate detailed spending reports in various formats (daily, weekly, monthly, yearly, or custom date ranges), filter by specific channels, or view overall spending.

Additional functionalities include natural language query support, optional slash command integration to perform actions like showing receipt data. All designed to streamline financial tracking by minimizing manual input and enabling efficient, structured querying of expense data.
session_items.Speaker: William Liu

session_items.Title: Natural Language Bridge to Legacy Email System
session_items.Description:
This project presents a great solution to one of modern communication's most persistent challenges: The continued widespread use of legacy email alongside newer messaging platforms. Despite the evolution of systems like Rocket.Chat, email remains deeply entrenched in global workflows and communities. This project elegantly bridges this divide by creating a seamless interface that allows Rocket.Chat users to interact with email systems through natural language commands, bringing legacy email functionality directly into the Rocket.Chat environment.

With the help of this app:
- User can send the email to anyone and generate email content too.
- User can summarise the conversations in channel/thread and send it as an email to anyone.
- User can get email statistics.
- User can send mass emails to people present in the channel.

session_items.Mentor: The Amazing ones 1. Zishan Ahmad 2. Yuriko Kikuchi
session_items.Description: Trip Helper App is a smart travel assistant that makes planning trips effortless and fun. The best part is that it uses a Large Language Model (LLM) extensively to understand user needs, and answer travel related questions instantly. This makes the app feel like you’re chatting with a knowledgeable travel buddy who’s always ready to help, saving you time and making your trips smoother and more enjoyable.
session_items.Speaker: Piyush Bhatt

session_items.Title: Code Review Assistant App for Rocket.Chat
session_items.Description: The Code Review Assistant App for Rocket.Chat is an AI-powered tool designed to streamline and accelerate the code review process in open-source projects. It analyzes pull requests, identifies the most suitable reviewers using commit history, the CODEOWNERS file, and contribution patterns, and automatically assigns them. The app also performs a preliminary review using LLMs and notifies relevant contributors via Rocket.Chat. It provides commands and reminders to ensure timely code review and collaboration. This tool improves the developer experience and helps open-source teams reduce PR delays.

session_items.Title: Real Time Message Rendering in Message Composer
session_items.Description:
The Rich Text Composer being developed will be able to show rich formatted text on the fly. Markdown formats enclosed between asterisks, underscores and tilde will show up as formatted rich text as soon as it is being typed.
Real time preview allows users to see the exact format that will finally render in the chat room. This project is being simultaneously developed alongside another Composer project which will allow AI generated text being generated on the fly.
This project can help bridge the gap between the limitations of typing plain text markdown inside a plain text editor, and simplifying the user experience by being able to create complex equations and code.
session_items.Speaker: Ishan Mitra

session_items.Title: Passkey-Based WebAuthn Authentication for Rocket.Chat
session_items.Description:
The WebAuthn standard, now widely available on modern Android and iOS devices, enable
convenient passwordless authentication satisfying 2FA (biometrics and "have device").
Frequently this involves scanning a QR code followed by unintrusive biometrics such as FaceID
on iOS. This project aims to integrate WebAuthn in Rocket.Chat authentication to offer a
passwordless, secure login experience. The implementation needs to be aligned with
Rocket.Chat’s existing authentication system while ensuring backward compatibility with all
existing login methods.
session_items.Speaker: Fang Zihao

session_items.Title: Fuselage React Native compatibility (tamagui)
session_items.Description:
The project focuses on modernizing the Fuselage component library by migrating selected Ul components to Tamagui a performant, design-system-driven React & React Native Ul kit. This allows Rocket.Chat's component library to support cross-platform rendering (web + native) from a single codebase.

The migration includes:

Rewriting core components like Button, Input, Card, and Autocomplete

Ensuring parity with the original @rocket.chat/fuselage APIs

Maintaining styling consistency via Tamagui tokens

Improving developer experience with Storybook integration for cross-platform testing

This initiative bridges the web-native gap, enabling future-ready development for Rocket.Chat.
session_items.Speaker: Thanisha Dewangan

session_items.Title: Log in via QR code using mobile app
session_items.Description:
This project introduces a modern, passwordless login experience for Rocket.Chat’s web client using QR codes and real-time communication. Instead of typing in credentials, users can now simply scan a QR code using the Rocket.Chat mobile app to log in instantly and securely.

Here’s how it works: When a user visits the web login page, they’re shown a short-lived, cryptographically signed QR code that refreshes every 60 seconds. An authenticated mobile user can scan this code using the in-app scanner, triggering a secure token validation process over WebSocket. If valid, the web client logs in immediately — no password, no email, no friction.

The system was built using React for the web UI, React Native for the scanner, and Node.js for backend validation and token handling. The key highlights include ephemeral token logic, real-time WebSocket communication, and secure mobile-to-web authentication flow.

It’s cool because it combines convenience and security in a way that feels seamless. For users, it's one-tap login. For Rocket.Chat, it's a robust and scalable solution that enhances UX without compromising safety.
session_items.Speaker: Jinendra Jain

session_items.Title: Implement visual regression testing
session_items.Description:
Visual regression testing is a relatively new and evolving field in software testing. Unlike traditional unit or integration tests, which validate logic and functionality, visual regression testing focuses on ensuring that the appearance of UI components remains consistent over time.
At Rocket.Chat and in its component library Fuselage, this is achieved using a tool called Loki.
Loki captures screenshots (snapshots) of UI components and compares the current rendering with a previously approved reference snapshot. It uses an image comparison library (like pixelmatch) to detect visual differences at the pixel level. If any visual discrepancy is found, Loki reports that the component has visually changed — this can help catch unintended UI regressions early in development.
Loki has option to run test inside a Docker container, which ensures that snapshots are taken in a consistent rendering environment . This is especially important when running in different environments , as it minimizes flakiness and platform-specific inconsistencies.
A smart system is in place to optimize the test scope:
If a component (e.g., Button) is changed, Loki doesn't just test that component.
It also tests:
Other components within the same package that might depend on the changed component.
Other packages with Storybook entries that import or use the changed component.
This approach ensures comprehensive coverage while still being efficient, as it avoids re-running all snapshots unnecessarily.
session_items.Speaker: Anshul

session_items.Title: End to End Testing using Maestro
session_items.Description:
My GSoC project at Rocket.Chat is about improving the testing system for the Rocket.Chat mobile app using a tool called Maestro. Maestro helps test the app by acting like a real user. It can tap buttons, type messages, switch between screens, and make sure everything works the way it should.

The goal of my project is to build and improve these tests so that developers can catch bugs early and be more confident when they update or release new features. I’m also connecting these tests to GitHub Actions, so they run automatically whenever someone makes a change to the app. This helps keep the app stable without needing to test everything manually.

While working on this project, I’m learning a lot about how end-to-end testing works, why testing is important, and how automated tests are used in real-world software development. I’m also learning how continuous integration tools like GitHub Actions help run these tests every time code is pushed.

This project is exciting because it helps improve the quality of the app, saves developers time, and gives users a better experience. It also gives me hands-on experience with testing tools, automation, and working on a real open-source project.
session_items.Speaker: Rohit Bansal

session_items.Title: Messages scheduling
session_items.Description:
This project introduces scheduled messaging to Rocket.Chat, allowing users to compose messages in advance and have them automatically delivered at a specific time. It's especially useful for teams spread across time zones, enabling communication to happen at the most effective moment—even if the sender is offline.

Whether it's for sending reminders, announcements, or time-sensitive updates, scheduled messaging gives users more control over when their messages are delivered. They can also review, update, or cancel scheduled messages before they're sent.

What makes this feature stand out is how it enhances asynchronous collaboration and helps reduce the pressure of real-time communication. By letting users plan their messages with precision, it promotes more thoughtful, efficient, and timely conversations across global teams.
session_items.Speaker: Thotsem Jajo

session_items.Title: Server Guide Agent
session_items.Description: This project focuses on building an intelligent onboarding and user guidance agent app within Rocket.Chat to enhance new user engagement. It introduces two main workflows — Admin Workflow and User Workflow , designed to simplify the onboarding process and provide personalized assistance to users. In the Admin Workflow, server administrators can configure key onboarding elements such as welcome messages, server rules, suggested channels, default channels for auto-joining, and guides for important features. Admins can also broadcast messages to multiple users and channels. In the User Workflow, regular users interact with the bot, which responds based on the admin-defined configurations. The bot assists users by answering questions about server rules, recommending useful channels, and guiding them through onboarding and many more.
session_items.Speaker: Abir Chakraborty

session_items.Title: Private Teams and Private Channels Administration Improvements
session_items.Description: This project enhances administrators’ ability to manage private teams and channels in Rocket.Chat. Authorized admins can add or remove users, change user roles, and manage team channels via the Directory, even if they are not members. The project aims to make it easier for platform administrators to monitor and intervene when necessary, while still respecting user privacy boundaries. This improves transparency, control, and flexibility in workspace management.
session_items.Speaker: Lexie Huang
